# Requirements

Neo is now the sole loop and identity, so the coding surface must be Neo's — but the /cody client is still wired to the retired codyd orchestrator (its own reducer, its own event vocabulary, a three-tier layout system beta users disliked, and a preview pane whose backend events never shipped). This feature replaces all of it with ONE workbench shaped like bolt.diy's celebrated UI (studied from the clone at /root/matrix/temp/bolt.diy): the chat rail is a real Neo conversation over the existing useChat reducer; a workbench slides in from the right with a Code / Diff / Preview slider; each turn's file writes and commands render as an inline artifact card in chat with live per-action status; the editor shows Neo typing live and is itself editable (CodeMirror, saved through a real workspace write API with an honest conflict posture); and previews plus unsafe execution run in on-demand Railway sandboxes, never on the main per-user VM. bolt.diy's structure is borrowed, not its code: we keep Next.js + Tailwind v4 tokens + the NeoTask reducer, reuse the already-good panes (react-arborist tree, @git-diff-view diff, xterm shell, the filmstrip idiom), and stay inside the house rules (background-contrast separation only, no borders for depth, no purple, no glow, no emojis). Locked with Andrew 2026-07-11: one workbench with no mode tiers; keep the /cody route rebranded to Neo; v1 flagship borrows = artifact cards + live preview + live-typing editor; editor is CodeMirror editable.

## Requirement 1: The coding route is a Neo conversation — codyd's client layer dies

**User Story:** As a user, I want the coding surface to be Neo — same brain, same memory, same stream — so that coding is not a separate sibling agent with a separate history.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE /cody route SHALL keep its mount (app/[locale]/cody/page.tsx) but its chat rail SHALL be a real Neo conversation driven by the existing useChat reducer and Neo event families (tool.step, chat.delta, chat.assistant, tool.todo) over the Neo daemon base path — not useCody/codyd.
2. THE codyd client layer SHALL be retired from the live surface: no live code path SHALL call lib/api/cody.ts run/intent routes (submitChat, getCodyTrace, stopRun, answerIntent, steerIntent) or the useCody reducer.
3. HISTORY SHALL be server-backed via Neo's conversation list filtered to the active project — the localStorage recent-runs stopgap (lib/cody/recent-runs.ts) SHALL be deleted.
4. THE surface SHALL carry Neo's identity in all copy and naming (no Cody-branded strings in the rendered UI).
5. A test SHALL prove the coding chat rail folds a real Neo event trace (live + reopen via buildTaskFromTrace) into the same state the dashboard would.

## Requirement 2: One workbench shell: slide-in panel with a Code / Diff / Preview slider

**User Story:** As a user, I want the workbench to appear when Neo starts producing work and to switch views without losing state, so that the surface feels like one machine rather than three layouts.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE tier system SHALL be retired: tiering.ts and the three layout files (layout-prototype/engineer/architect) SHALL have no live consumers; ONE workbench layout SHALL serve all users.
2. THE workbench SHALL slide in from the right when work steps arrive (and via a manual toggle), full-width on small viewports, with the chat rail remaining the primary column.
3. A three-position Code / Diff / Preview slider SHALL switch panels that stay mounted (no unmount flash); a terminal panel SHALL be toggleable within the workbench.
4. THE shell SHALL follow house rules on the existing token ladder (bg-surface-* separation, single accent, no border strokes for depth, no glow/emoji/purple); the pre-existing border-stroke violations in neo-workspace.tsx (border border-zinc-800/70 in BrowserView/EditorView) SHALL be fixed to surface tokens.
5. A test SHALL prove slider switching preserves panel state (open file, scroll/diff selection) across view changes.

## Requirement 3: Artifact/action cards: each turn's work renders inline in chat with live per-action status

**User Story:** As a user, I want a collapsible card in chat showing exactly what Neo is doing — each file write and command with a live status — so that I can follow the work without opening the workbench.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a turn produces editor/terminal/preview steps, THE chat rail SHALL fold them into one collapsible artifact card per turn: header from Neo's narration, one row per action (file path or command) with a live status icon (pending/running/complete/failed).
2. THE per-action status SHALL reflect real transitions emitted by the daemon on the step events (running then done/failed), not synthesized client-side timing.
3. CLICKING a file row SHALL open that file in the workbench Code view; clicking a command row SHALL reveal the terminal panel.
4. CARDS SHALL be durable: trace replay on reopen SHALL rebuild them with final statuses.
5. A test SHALL prove a real event sequence renders a card whose rows transition status live and rebuild identically from the trace.

## Requirement 4: Workspace API on the Neo daemon: read, write, diff, exec

**User Story:** As the workbench, I want the daemon to expose the project workspace, so that the tree, editor, diff, and terminal are backed by the real VM filesystem.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE Neo daemon SHALL expose project-scoped workspace endpoints: file tree, file read, file WRITE (for the editable editor), diff, and bounded command exec — auth-gated the same way as /media.
2. ALL paths SHALL normalize through a single seam that rejects workspace escapes (the edit.Rel posture: absolute or ../ paths never reach the filesystem outside the project root).
3. FILE writes SHALL be atomic (write-then-rename or equivalent) and SHALL return the resulting file version/hash so the client can detect staleness.
4. A test SHALL prove read/write/diff/exec round-trips against a real workspace directory, and that escape attempts are rejected.

## Requirement 5: File tree + editable CodeMirror editor + diff, with an honest conflict posture

**User Story:** As a user, I want to browse, read, and directly edit the project files with unsaved-change indicators, so that I can fix small things myself without a chat round-trip.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE Code view SHALL compose the existing react-arborist tree (cody-tree.tsx) with a CodeMirror 6 editor (language packs per extension); the Diff view SHALL reuse CodyDiffView (@git-diff-view + Shiki) fed by the daemon diff endpoint.
2. USER edits SHALL save through the workspace write API; dirty buffers SHALL show unsaved dots on the tree and the tab.
3. WHEN Neo writes a file the user has unsaved local edits to, THE editor SHALL NOT silently clobber the buffer — it SHALL surface the conflict with a diff and an explicit take-Neo's/keep-mine choice; WHILE Neo is actively writing a file, that file's editor SHALL be read-only.
4. A test SHALL prove save round-trips to disk, unsaved indicators track buffer state, and the conflict path never loses user bytes without an explicit choice.

## Requirement 6: Live-typing editor: file writes stream into the open editor

**User Story:** As a user, I want to watch Neo type into the editor as it writes a file, so that the workbench feels alive and I can react early.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN Neo writes a file, THE daemon SHALL stream bounded file-content deltas on the step event channel so the client renders progressive content in the editor; the final persisted step SHALL carry the complete state.
2. WHEN a file write begins, THE workbench SHALL auto-open (if hidden), switch to Code view, and select that file — matching bolt.diy's force-follow behavior — unless the user has pinned a different view this run.
3. STREAMING SHALL be bounded (delta size/rate caps) and best-effort: a dropped delta stream degrades to the final content, never a corrupted buffer.
4. A test SHALL prove a real streamed write renders progressively and converges byte-identical to the file on disk.

## Requirement 7: Preview via on-demand Railway sandboxes, surfaced as durable preview events

**User Story:** As a user, I want a real running preview of my app in the workbench, so that I can see what Neo built without trusting the main VM to run unsafe code.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a preview is requested (by Neo or the user), THE daemon SHALL provision an on-demand Railway sandbox, sync the project workspace into it, start the dev command, and health-poll until serving — the main per-user VM SHALL NOT run the dev server.
2. THE lifecycle SHALL surface as durable events (preview.pending / preview.ready with URL / preview.failed with reason / preview.expired) whitelisted in traceWorkspaceTypes so reopen rebuilds the last preview state honestly.
3. THE Preview pane SHALL render the sandbox URL in an iframe with bolt.diy's chrome: editable address-bar path, reload, and open-in-new-tab; failure and expiry states SHALL be honest empty/error states, never a stale frame presented as live.
4. SANDBOXES SHALL be bounded: idle expiry tears them down, and a per-user concurrent-sandbox cap holds.
5. A test SHALL prove the controller lifecycle (pending → ready → expired) against a real HTTP dev-server target, event durability across reopen, and the cap/expiry bounds.

## Requirement 8: Projects on the Neo daemon, rebrand, and dead-code removal

**User Story:** As a user, I want my projects list to keep working under Neo with a clean surface, so that the transition is invisible except for the improvement.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. PROJECTS SHALL remain workspace subdirectories with a minimal registry on the Neo daemon (list/create/rename/archive/delete) replacing codyd's project routes; conversations SHALL be tagged with a project id so Workspace and History scope per project.
2. THE shell (cody-app/cody-sidebar/cody-topbar) SHALL be rebranded to Neo identity end-to-end (copy, i18n keys across all 5 locales).
3. DEAD code SHALL be deleted, not stranded: useCody.ts, the codyd routes in lib/api/cody.ts, tiering.ts, the three layouts, cody-run-parts.tsx, cody-activity.tsx, cody-code-panes.tsx, cody-architect-panes.tsx, recent-runs.ts — the build SHALL be green with zero imports of them.
4. A test/check SHALL prove the client builds green (tsc, eslint, vitest) after removal and no rendered string carries the retired Cody branding.

## Requirement 9: No-fakes end-to-end proof of the Neo workbench

**User Story:** As the owner, I want the whole instrument proven on the real system, so that the beta users' replacement surface is demonstrated, not asserted.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. AN end-to-end proof SHALL drive a REAL Neo run that writes files and runs commands in a real project workspace, asserting: artifact card rows transition through real statuses; the editor receives the live-typed content and converges with disk; the diff endpoint reflects the changes; and reopen rebuilds cards + workbench from the trace.
2. THE preview path SHALL be proven against the real controller with a real serving target, including honest failure and expiry states.
3. NO test in this feature SHALL substitute a fake for a real code path: real tool dispatch, real workspace files, real event stream and trace replay, and the real client reducer throughout.
